aspects.says: An abstract class can't be instantiated, but its constructor runs for every subclass, anonymous ones included, so the checks every subclass needs go there.
basis: section:An Abstract Class Can't Be Instantiated, but Its Constructor Runs for Every Subclass

aspects.says: A default method gives old implementations a body, so they keep running and still compile.
basis: section:Adding an Abstract Method to a Published Interface Breaks Every Implementer; a Default Method Doesn't

aspects.says: An interface with exactly one abstract method, not counting public methods of Object, is functional with or without @FunctionalInterface; the annotation makes javac reject a second abstract method at the interface.
basis: section:A Functional Interface Is the Lightest Abstraction: One Abstract Method, and Any Lambda Implements It

aspects.says: Every field of an interface is public static final, so a mutable object declared there is one shared value for every implementation, and per-object state needs an abstract class.
basis: section:An Interface Can't Hold an Object's State: a Field Declared There Is One Constant for Every Implementation

aspects.says: An interface has no instance fields, constructors or protected members, and its static methods are not inherited; an abstract class has all of these but takes a class's one superclass.
basis: section:An Interface Can't Hold an Object's State: a Field Declared There Is One Constant for Every Implementation
aspects.reason: what javac accepts in each kind of type has no wrong solution that compiles; the quiz asks about the shared field, and the Reference lists the compile errors

aspects.says: List does not promise what get(i) costs: it walks the links on a LinkedList, so code over any List iterates, and uses indexes only on a RandomAccess list.
basis: section:An Abstraction Hides Its Cost Too: List.get(i) Is O(n) on a LinkedList

aspects.says: Adding an abstract method to a published interface makes implementers fail to compile when rebuilt, and old binaries throw AbstractMethodError at the first call of the method.
basis: section:Adding an Abstract Method to a Published Interface Breaks Every Implementer; a Default Method Doesn't
